name: Primo Packaging
old_description: As a trusted manufacturer and converter, Primo Packaging produces durable, customizable plastic bags designed to meet your exact specifications. From raw material to finished product, every step of our process is engineered for consistency, efficiency, and quality.
about:
Primo Packaging operates from a facility on North Orange Blossom Trail in Orlando, Florida. The company's founding date and ownership structure have not been publicly disclosed.

The company functions as a manufacturer and converter of flexible plastic packaging, producing custom bags and pouches for a range of end uses. Its process capabilities include eight-color process printing, four lamination methods (solvent, extrusion, dry, and co-extrusion), and the fabrication of numerous bag styles such as stand-up pouches, wicketed bags, poly mailers, gusseted bags, and vacuum pouches. Materials processed span polyethylene, polypropylene, BOPP, CPP, PET, PVDC, nylon, and specialty co-extruded films, supplied as roll stock or converted into finished bags.

Primo Packaging serves customers in confectionery, bakeries, snack foods, pet products, meat and fish processing, agriculture, and landscaping, among other sectors. The company does not publish a client list, but its stated industry focus indicates a broad base of food and non-food packagers.

According to its own description, Primo Packaging engineers every step from raw material to finished product for consistency, efficiency, and quality, positioning itself as a partner for brands that require precise graphics and reliable packaging performance.

name: Printex Fabrics, Inc

about:
Printex Fabrics, Inc. operates from Honolulu, Hawaii, where it has been a fixture in the local textile scene since 2000. The company was founded as a specialist in Polynesian print fabrics that are unique to the islands, positioning itself as Hawaii’s textile supplier. Ownership details and founder names are not disclosed.

The business functions as a wholesaler of Hawaiian print and design fabrics, offering a broad assortment that includes poly‑cotton blends, 100 % cotton, 100 % rayon, and 100 % cotton canvas. Its catalog spans traditional palaka yarn‑dye twills, seersucker, barkcloth, shirting, microfiber, sheeting, batting, pillow inserts, scuba knits, and polyfill, along with a rotating selection of new proprietary designs.

Printex serves the wholesale market, supplying retailers, designers, and manufacturers who need authentic Hawaiian prints for apparel, home décor, and craft applications. The company’s emphasis on island‑specific patterns makes it a go‑to source for buyers seeking culturally rooted textiles.

The firm says its point of difference lies in “covering the world in Aloha” through both traditional and contemporary designs that express Hawaii’s history, culture, and arts, a mission that has guided its product development for over two decades.

name: Priority Plastics Inc
old_description: We invest in our people, equipment and technology to bring you the best packaging solutions available through quality, timeliness, relationships and sustainability.
about:
Priority Plastics Inc. is headquartered in Grand Prairie, Texas, and operates extrusion blow‑molding facilities across the United States. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in public materials.

The company manufactures plastic packaging solutions including HDPE and PET containers, tight‑head pails, canisters, and dry‑pack towel wipes. Core processes are extrusion blow molding and injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), the latter marketed as a way to expand PET applications. A multi‑plant footprint enables coast‑to‑coast production, multi‑plant sourcing, and in‑plant customer‑service support. The firm also develops custom tooling and maintains an expanding library of stock tools to shorten lead times.

Priority Plastics serves customers ranging from startups to multinational firms in food and beverage, nutrition and wellness, industrial, personal care, agriculture, animal health, cannabis/hemp/CBD, hardware, hazardous materials, healthcare/nutraceuticals, and specialty chemicals.

The company emphasizes four pillars—quality, timeliness, relationships, and sustainability. Its GreenLite platform incorporates post‑consumer recycled (PCR) content and lightweight designs; the PriorityPour ECO line uses up to 80 % recycled core material. Public targets include sourcing 60 % of materials from recycled or renewable sources by 2035, making 80 % of products recyclable by 2028, and cutting Scope 2 and 3 emissions 30 % by 2030. All facilities recycle unused resin, and the geographically distributed network is positioned to lower freight costs and carbon emissions.

name: Private Label Specialties
old_description: Uplevel Your Customer Experience & Profits With Branded Beverages.
about:
Private Label Specialties is based in Goffstown, New Hampshire, and was founded in 1991 by Ray Duhaime, who serves as president. The company began with a simple idea: offering custom-labeled sparkling water as an alternative to national brands like Poland Spring and Perrier, giving businesses a way to put their own name on a beverage.

In 1997 it added promotional products distribution, and in 2006–2007 brought screen printing, embroidery, and direct-to-garment printing in-house by acquiring its former vendor. The operation now runs a full-service apparel decoration shop alongside beverage production, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

The customer base spans restaurants, pizzerias, sub shops, catering companies, country stores, farm stands, and broader hospitality and service-based industries. Clients use the branded beverages for resale or as promotional giveaways, while the apparel and promo items (drawn from a catalog of over 750,000 products) support broader marketing programs.

The company says its “Unique Branding Advantage” rests on a trifecta of excellent price, impeccable quality, and outstanding service. Investments in technology allow it to move from concept to finished label in under an hour, and the founder’s original goal—helping businesses market themselves rather than big brands—remains the stated mission.

name: Pro AG Equipment
old_description: Founded in 1948 as Lockwood Corp. grand forks and transitioning to Pro Ag Equipment 1982.
about:
Pro AG Equipment traces its roots to 1948 when Lockwood Corp. was established in Grand Forks, North Dakota. The business transitioned to its current name, Pro Ag Equipment, in 1982. Headquartered in Grafton, North Dakota, the company operates three locations: Grand Forks and Grafton in North Dakota, and Hastings in Florida. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company functions primarily as a distributor of short-line equipment tailored for sugar beet, bean, and potato farming. Beyond new equipment sales, Pro Ag Equipment supplies parts, liquid fertilizer components, and provides repair services. It also performs manufacturing, though the scope of in-house production is not detailed. The multi-location footprint supports a regional supply chain for agricultural operators.

Pro Ag Equipment serves growers and agricultural operations specializing in sugar beet, bean, and potato production. Its customer base includes farms and dealers requiring equipment, replacement parts, fertilizer system components, and maintenance support. The company's geographic presence in the Red River Valley and Florida positions it to serve major sugar beet and potato growing regions.

The company highlights a special annual service sale as a recurring customer benefit. Its longevity since 1948 and evolution from Lockwood Corp. reflect a focus on adapting to the equipment needs of specialty crop farmers.

name: Pro-Forming Sheet Metal LLC
old_description: We offer our Metal Custom Fabrication customers superior supplemental Metal Machining and Milling
about:
Pro-Forming Sheet Metal LLC operates from Norwich, Connecticut, where it has provided custom metal fabrication and machining services for more than 25 years. The shop began as a metal fabrication business and has since expanded its capabilities to include CNC punching, forming, welding, machining, and finishing.

The company offers a range of metal fabrication processes including CNC turret punching (30-ton, 25-station), CNC press brake forming (120-ton, 10-foot), roll forming, sawing, plasma and oxy-acetylene cutting, MIG and TIG welding, and basic machining such as milling, drilling, and turning. It also provides in-house wet painting, mechanical and turnkey assembly, prototyping, and machinery rebuilding. Pro-Forming handles short, medium, and long production runs, working with steel, stainless steel, aluminum, cast iron, and bronze.

Pro-Forming serves manufacturers in Connecticut and across the United States, producing parts such as precision brackets with tight tolerances and heavy-duty frames designed to support 30,000-pound machinery. Its customer base includes businesses needing custom metal fabrication, machining, and assembly services.

The company emphasizes a one-stop-shop approach, combining CAD design, CNC punching, forming, welding, machining, and finishing under one roof to control lead times and costs. It highlights its experienced craftsmen, with an average of over 20 years of industry experience, and its ability to hold tolerances to the thousandth of an inch.

name: Pro-Tech Power Sales
old_description: Copyright © 2025 Pro-Tech Power Sales, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
about:
Pro-Tech Power Sales, Inc. is based in Roseville, Minnesota. The company operates as a manufacturers' representative and distributor for power industry equipment across the Upper Midwest and into Canada.

The firm's product portfolio centers on condition monitoring and hardware for electric power transmission and distribution systems. It represents the Doble family of online monitoring products for transformers and bushings, Morgan Schaffer dissolved gas analysis (DGA) products and services, and a range of transmission structures including wood crossarms, braces, hardware, and fiberglass brackets. It also supplies transmission and distribution line hardware along with current and voltage line sensors.

Pro-Tech serves electric utilities, contractors, and engineering firms throughout Colorado, Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and the Canadian provinces of Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, and the Maritimes. Its territory coverage reflects a focus on the northern U.S. and central Canadian power markets.

The company emphasizes broad product availability and technical support for the brands it represents, though specific founding details, ownership structure, and certifications are not publicly disclosed.

name: ProCare Medical Equipment
old_description: ProCare Medical Equipment specializes in the rental of durable
about:
ProCare Medical Equipment was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Meridian, Idaho. The company began as a medical equipment provider focused on serving patient care facilities in the region.

ProCare specializes in the rental, sale, and servicing of durable medical equipment (DME) for healthcare facilities. Its services include equipment rental programs, repair and preventative maintenance on most brands, cleaning and sanitization under its proprietary Patient Ready Certified™ program, liquid oxygen delivery with respiratory therapy support, and continuing education for healthcare professionals. The company also assembles custom equipment packages tailored to skilled nursing, hospice, rehabilitation, and VA facilities.

ProCare serves long-term care facilities, rehabilitation and transitional care centers, hospice agencies, and VA or government healthcare facilities across Idaho and eastern Oregon. Its customer base includes skilled nursing facilities seeking wound care and bariatric equipment, hospice providers needing comfort-focused surfaces and bed frames, and government facilities requiring respiratory and rehabilitation solutions.

The company emphasizes compassionate, on-time service and a holistic approach called 360° Servicing, which integrates rental, repair, cleaning, and education into a single solution. Its Patient Ready Certified™ seal guarantees equipment sanitized beyond industry standards, and its Sunrise Sessions provide continuing education for clinical staff. ProCare states its mission is to empower health with innovative solutions and to become the primary DME provider for professional care agencies in its service area.

name: ProStock Auto Parts - Saddle Brook
old_description: We’re a leading supplier to the Professional Installer of auto parts and equipment in New Jersey, New York and Connecticut.
about:
ProStock Automotive operates from its corporate office in Saddle Brook, New Jersey, where it has served the tri-state automotive aftermarket for more than 30 years. The locally owned company maintains a network of 12 locations across northern New Jersey, New York, and Connecticut, including branches in East Hanover, Midland Park, Montclair, Ridgefield, Waterbury, and Totowa.

The distributor supplies professional installers with a curated selection of brand-name parts for domestic, Asian, and European vehicles, carrying lines such as Denso, Bosch, Gates, Moog, and Delco. A company-owned fleet of GPS-tracked vehicles runs on a dispatched delivery system, staffed by long-tenured drivers who provide consistent daily service to repair shops. Counter operations are handled by more than 25 specialists, each averaging two decades of experience, supported by 24/7 online ordering through ACDelco Connect, NexPart, Parts Tech, and the company's own WebLink catalog.

Customers range from independent repair shops to fleet maintenance operations throughout the New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut market. The company emphasizes quality over price substitution, with buyers selecting brands to ensure installers can work with confidence. Returns are processed through a dedicated department that issues credits via fax or email within 24 hours.

Founded on the principle of "Professional service, always in stock," ProStock positions itself as large enough to offer competitive pricing and inventory depth while remaining small enough to respond to individual shop needs. The business model combines local inventory availability with digital ordering tools that allow technicians to look up parts by VIN or license plate from a smartphone.

name: Process Ohio Corporation
old_description: Your Source for Material Handlers, Attachments & Recycling Equipment
about:
Process Equipment, based in New Waterford, Ohio, operates as an independent dealer of material handlers, attachments, and recycling equipment. The company has served the scrap, recycling, waste, demolition, port, and industrial material-handling sectors for over three decades, building a reputation for supplying work-ready machinery from major OEMs.

The company stocks a large inventory of new, used, and rebuilt material handlers from brands such as Caterpillar, Sennebogen, Liebherr, and Fuchs, along with attachments including orange-peel grapples from Rotobec, Pro-Lift, and Kinshofer, as well as magnets and shredders from Wolf and Hammel. Process Equipment buys each machine, subjects it to a 210-point internal inspection supplemented by third-party verification, and then offers it with installation support, parts supply, and service. New inventory arrives weekly, and the company arranges nationwide and international shipping.

Customers include scrap yards, materials recovery facilities, timber and lumber mills, port terminals, demolition contractors, and steel mills. Typical applications cover scrap and metal recycling, waste transfer and MRF operations, bulk material handling at ports, and timber yard processing.

Process Equipment distinguishes itself by not acting as a broker; it takes ownership of every unit, reconditions it to a consistent quality standard, and provides transparent documentation such as video walkthroughs, detailed photo packages, and fluid analysis. The goal is to deliver a purchasing experience close to buying new without the new-machine price, backed by independent, expert advice.
